reading.body:
CyrusOne Wappingers Falls is a 3 MW IT capacity data center in the Hudson Valley, north of New York City. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, this is roughly 75 racks of compute. The facility holds SSAE 16 Type II certification, which qualifies it for handling sensitive workloads requiring audited security controls. The 100,000 square feet of technical space suggests a mid-scale regional campus built for enterprise and cloud tenants rather than hyperscale AI infrastructure.

This is the only data center in New York State with published IT capacity on operator spec pages that this site has mapped, giving it nominal rank one among disclosed facilities in the state. The state context shows 31 mapped facilities total, but 30 do not publish power figures, making Wappingers Falls unrepresentative of actual regional capacity. New York State's true AI-relevant infrastructure is not visible in operator disclosures.

For AI scaling decisions, this campus is not material. 3 MW is beneath the minimum scale of modern AI training clusters and represents legacy enterprise colocation, not the power-dense infrastructure now driving accelerator placement. It sits in the Northeast regional market but lacks the published power density, cooling specification, or grid headroom data needed to assess its role in AI workload routing. Without similar disclosures from the other 30 facilities in the state, New York's actual data center capacity for AI remains opaque.
